chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two, peace be upon them, who said:
I asked him about tayammum, and he said: “Twice, twice for the face and the hands.”

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: tayammum; dry ablution performed as a substitute for wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.الْوَجْهِ: the face; one of the parts wiped in tayammum
key_terms.الْيَدَيْنِ: the hands; one of the parts wiped in tayammum
key_terms.مَرَّتَيْنِ: twice; indicating the number of times the action is performed

ai.seo_question: How should tayammum be performed for the face and hands according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the manner of tayammum. It indicates performing two applications for the face and the hands, and it is part of the jurisprudence of ritual purity and worship in cases where tayammum is required.
